messages:

Cc: Alex Chang <alex@datacorp.com>, procurement@datacorp.com
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly bulk runs - exception for completion window and retries

Vanessa,

We're seeing a growing fraction of our nightly bulk inference jobs slip outside the 3-hour completion window you have in the baseline SLA. The load spike on our data ingestion side means a long-tailed distribution for some batches (large customer segments + long sequences).

Given our compliance timelines, we need a short-term carveout that: 1) extends the nightly completion window to 5 hours for a defined subset of job classes, and 2) confirms safe retry semantics so that our downstream dedupe isn't broken (idempotency keys across attempts).

Two asks: can Redwood provide a written proposal (SLA amendment or ride-along carveout) with the operational controls you would require (backoff/hedging recommendations, idempotency guarantees, monitoring hooks)? Also we need an indication if this will affect uptime/latency commitments or credits.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Ops, DataCorp Analytics

Subject: Re: Nightly bulk runs - exception for completion window and retries

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and sample log. We can absolutely put together a formal carveout proposal. High level:

- Proposal: 5-hour nightly completion window for "large-segment" class jobs for a defined trial period (90 days) with agreed sampling/alerts.
- Idempotency: require a stable idempotency key on your side + our recommended safe-retry semantics (exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts = 5). We will provide a client-side SDK snippet and a server-side semantics doc.
- Credits & uptime: this carveout would be an operational SLA exception rather than a change to platform-wide uptime SLOs. If the exception is accepted we will include a remediation plan and clearly defined credit triggers for late completions beyond the carveout window.

I'm attaching a first-draft writeup (nightly-grace-draft.pdf) and an attempt matrix for Marcus and Karthik to review. Can Marcus comment on any engine-level constraints that would make the hedging pattern unsafe? Karthik — does product need any additional gating (rollout windows, config flags) to enable this for your account?

I'll also coordinate with Neha on the commercial language re: credits. If you prefer, let's set a 30-minute call Monday to run the plan and timelines.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks for looping me in — quick technical read:

- Long tail cause: observed correlation between input sequence-length variance and KV-cache pressure in multi-tenant pools. For very large sequences the per-token latency increases nonlinearly.
- Safe retry pattern we recommend: client must include an idempotency_key per logical job (not per shard). Server will store job terminal states for 72 hours. Retry behavior: exponential backoff (base=2s) with capped jitter, max 5 attempts. If a retry hits a mid-execution preemption (eviction) we return a 409 with a "retryable" header.
- Hedging (sending duplicate attempts to different backends) is possible but only for fully idempotent jobs and when your payload includes a deterministic checksum. Hedging increases resource usage and would need a scoped quota exception.
- Operational controls: request-level tracing headers (X-DC-job-id), per-job timeout config, and a small prefix cache for repeated prompt prefixes to reduce tail risk for near-duplicate batches.

I've updated the matrix in the attached spreadsheet with expected cost delta estimates under hedging vs backoff. Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: idempotency-retry-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)]
